source_text: Sed invidendo tibi, in quadam meridie compertae veritatis sine obumbramento ignorationis - ut loqueris - insanimus qui vel supersederunt scienda cognoscere, vel non formidant ignorata culpare
pass_a_gloss: But invidendo to-you, in quadam meridie compertae of-truth without obumbramento ignorationis - so-that/as loqueris - insanimus who or supersederunt scienda cognoscere, or not formidant ignorata culpare.
pass_b_english: Those who either neglected to learn what ought to be known, or are unafraid to condemn what they do not know.
In the noonday of discovered truth, without the shadow of ignorance, you rave through envy of me.
Envy immediately torments the very author from whom it arises.
One and the same vice cannot be both sin and punishment for sin.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
